label: BLESSED_1: a primitive predicate for having in itself the perfect good of an intellectual nature
term: most blessed (in se et ex se beatissimus; Lean `Primitives.MostBlessed`)
definition: PRIMITIVE. MostBlessed g: g has, in and from itself, the perfect good of an intellectual nature. After ST I q.26 a.1 (beatitude is the perfect good of an intellectual nature, and belongs to God in the highest degree). Counterexample: a stone (no intellectual nature); a human being in this life (an intellectual nature without its perfect good).
note: Explicitly identified primitive (Encode first). Open semantic obligation: a typed account of beatitude as possession of an intellectual nature's perfect good. Two open bridges constrain it, each giving a sufficient condition: 'Whatever is PERFECT_2 and HAS_INTELLECT_1 is BLESSED_1' and the weaker sense bridge 'Whatever is BLESSED_2 is BLESSED_1' (a23dd1ac), from the typed sibling BLESSED_2 (d0b7b32b: intellect, universal perfection, goodness as to being and act in understanding; disambiguation 70f4f510). Ex se, self-knowledge of one's sufficiency and formal understanding remain untyped.
